<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="אלול_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518920519_theRebbe_475" batchId="meluket-_D7_90_D7_9C_D7_95_D7_9C_meluket__BH_POST_1766518920519_theRebbe_475__p003">
  <section v="6">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that giving charity to a poor person enlivens them, which in turn arouses the enlivening of the lower spiritual worlds (Biya) and ultimately draws the revelation of Ein Sof's "face" during prayer.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">4)</t>
    <t s="1">And to understand in more detail the superiority of charity, about which our sages said: Rabbi Elazar would give a coin to a poor person and then pray, as it is stated, "I will behold Your face in righteousness,"</t>
    <t s="2">Now,</t>
    <t s="3">the concept of charity is to revive the spirit of the lowly,</t>
    <t s="4">that is, the poor person who has nothing,</t>
    <t s="5">and when one gives him charity, he enlivens him,</t>
    <t s="6">and through this, he also arouses above the matter of reviving the spirit of the lowly,</t>
    <t s="7">which are the three worlds of Beriah, Yetzirah, and Asiyah,</t>
    <t s="8">which are called "lowly,"</t>
    <t s="9">because the source of their coming into being is only from the aspect of Malchus, which is an aspect of mere illumination,</t>
    <t s="10">as it is written,</t>
    <t s="11">"For His Name is exalted alone"</t>
    <t s="12">(and only)</t>
    <t s="13">"His glory"</t>
    <t s="14">(which is merely radiance and illumination)</t>
    <t s="15">"is upon earth and heaven,"</t>
    <t s="16">and therefore it is necessary to revive the spirit of the lowly,</t>
    <t s="17">meaning,</t>
    <t s="18">that even in Biya, the light of Atzilus should be felt,</t>
    <t s="19">and this is the concept of charity above, which is effected by charity below.</t>
    <t s="20">And through this, afterward in prayer, there is drawn a revelation of light that transcends the chain of descent,</t>
    <t s="21">which is the matter of the illumination of Ein Sof from the aspect of "face,"</t>
    <t s="22">"I will behold Your face."</t>
  </section>
  <section v="7">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section details two modes of charity work—giving a coin to a poor person and appeasing him—explaining that the former draws the light of Atzilus to Biya, while the latter draws the inner aspect of G-dliness, corresponding to the eleven blessings.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And in more detail, regarding the matter of charity itself, there are two modes of service.</t>
    <t s="1">For our sages said,</t>
    <t s="2">"One who gives a coin to a poor person is blessed with six blessings, and one who appeases him is blessed with eleven blessings."</t>
    <t s="3">And the explanation of this is,</t>
    <t s="4">that giving a coin to a poor person is for his bodily needs,</t>
    <t s="5">and since through this he enlivens only his body,</t>
    <t s="6">then also his activity in the matter of charity above is only to draw the light of Atzilus into Biya.</t>
    <t s="7">And this is also hinted at in the word "coin" (prutah),</t>
    <t s="8">which is "detail" (perat) and "heh,"</t>
    <t s="9">meaning to draw and detail the aspect of the vav into the heh,</t>
    <t s="10">as explained in the Siddur,</t>
    <t s="11">in the discourse "Adon-ai, open my lips," regarding the matter of voice and speech,</t>
    <t s="12">that the voice is an aspect of generality,</t>
    <t s="13">and speech is an aspect of detail, which details what is in the general,</t>
    <t s="14">for the voice is an aspect of encompassing all the letters,</t>
    <t s="15">and the letters are an aspect of particularity, etc.</t>
    <t s="16">And this is the concept of "coin" (prutah)—to detail the aspect of the vav into the heh.</t>
    <t s="17">Therefore, he is blessed with six blessings,</t>
    <t s="18">corresponding to the letter vav of the Name Havayah.</t>
    <t s="19">However,</t>
    <t s="20">appeasing the poor person is not a matter needed only for his body,</t>
    <t s="21">but rather a matter of calming his mind,</t>
    <t s="22">meaning,</t>
    <t s="23">that the poor person, in himself, is in a state of bitterness, etc.,</t>
    <t s="24">because he has a complaint about the fact that he is poor,</t>
    <t s="25">as it is written,</t>
    <t s="26">"A prayer of the afflicted when he wraps himself," etc.,</t>
    <t s="27">that his prayer is about the very fact of his being poor,</t>
    <t s="28">for although the order of creation is such that there must be a distinction between rich and poor,</t>
    <t s="29">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="30">he argues why he must be the poor one.</t>
    <t s="31">And when one speaks to the heart of the poor person and calms his mind, etc., until he is appeased,</t>
    <t s="32">this is a matter more elevated than merely giving a coin for his bodily needs.</t>
    <t s="33">Therefore, through this, one effects</t>
    <t s="34">(not only the drawing of the light of Atzilus into Biya,</t>
    <t s="35">but also)</t>
    <t s="36">the drawing of the inner aspect of G-dliness.</t>
    <t s="37">And this is that one who appeases him is blessed with eleven blessings,</t>
    <t s="38">as is known, that the number eleven indicates an aspect that transcends the ten Sefiros,</t>
    <t s="39">similar to "before Havayah,"</t>
    <t s="40">above Havayah.</t>
    <t s="41">And this is also that "appeasement" (piyus) has the same letters as "Yosef,"</t>
    <t s="42">for regarding Yosef it is written,</t>
    <t s="43">"These are the generations of Yaakov, Yosef,"</t>
    <t s="44">meaning,</t>
    <t s="45">that the matter of Yaakov is in Atzilus,</t>
    <t s="46">but the purpose is that it be drawn also into Biya,</t>
    <t s="47">and this is the matter of Yosef, who is the provider of bread to all the land,</t>
    <t s="48">which is the concept of drawing downward,</t>
    <t s="49">and in order for it to be drawn downward, the drawing must be from a most elevated aspect, etc.</t>
    <t s="50">And this is the concept of "he would give a coin to a poor person and then pray,"</t>
    <t s="51">meaning that first there must be "he would give a coin,"</t>
    <t s="52">and through this, afterward one comes to "I will behold Your face,"</t>
    <t s="53">an inner drawing,</t>
    <t s="54">as through the matter of appeasement.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="8">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that both modes of charity must precede prayer, and that prayer involves two levels—external prostration (accepting the yoke) and internal prostration (perception)—corresponding to the two modes of charity.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">5)</t>
    <t s="1">And now, the two aforementioned modes in the service of charity</t>
    <t s="2">(one who gives a coin to a poor person and one who appeases him)</t>
    <t s="3">must be before prayer.</t>
    <t s="4">And the explanation of this is,</t>
    <t s="5">Now,</t>
    <t s="6">regarding prayer, our sages said,</t>
    <t s="7">"The Patriarchs instituted the prayers,"</t>
    <t s="8">and likewise our sages said,</t>
    <t s="9">that the three pilgrimage festivals correspond to the three Patriarchs,</t>
    <t s="10">Pesach corresponding to Avraham,</t>
    <t s="11">Shavuos corresponding to Yitzchak,</t>
    <t s="12">and Sukkos corresponding to Yaakov.</t>
    <t s="13">And it follows,</t>
    <t s="14">that the matter of prayer and the matter of the pilgrimage festivals are of one level.</t>
    <t s="15">And now,</t>
    <t s="16">regarding the pilgrimage festivals, it is written,</t>
    <t s="17">"Three times a year, all your males shall appear before the face of Havayah your G-d in the place He will choose,"</t>
    <t s="18">meaning,</t>
    <t s="19">that in the Holy Temple, which was aligned opposite the Heichalos,</t>
    <t s="20">there was a revelation of "the face of Havayah your G-d,"</t>
    <t s="21">and likewise in prayer, whose order was established corresponding to the Heichalos,</t>
    <t s="22">there is within it the revelation of "the face of Havayah your G-d."</t>
    <t s="23">And now,</t>
    <t s="24">the revelation of "the face of Havayah your G-d" in the Holy Temple was effected through the matter of prostration,</t>
    <t s="25">as it is written, "to see and to prostrate oneself," etc.</t>
    <t s="26">And regarding the matter of prostration, there are two aspects.</t>
    <t s="27">External prostration, which is like the prostration of a servant before the master, which is in a manner of coercion and compulsion,</t>
    <t s="28">such that it is possible that he has no desire for this at all,</t>
    <t s="29">but rather prostrates himself out of fear of the master,</t>
    <t s="30">in a manner of accepting the yoke.</t>
    <t s="31">And internal prostration, which is in an aspect of desire and will,</t>
    <t s="32">and in a manner that all his powers are nullified, etc.</t>
    <t s="33">And these two aspects in the matter of prostration are analogous to the two aspects of hearing and sight,</t>
    <t s="34">meaning,</t>
    <t s="35">that when the service is only an aspect of hearing,</t>
    <t s="36">this effects only external prostration,</t>
    <t s="37">but when the service is in an aspect of sight,</t>
    <t s="38">this effects internal prostration.</t>
    <t s="39">And likewise, in prayer there are these two matters,</t>
    <t s="40">for,</t>
    <t s="41">prayer is "a ladder set upon the earth," etc.,</t>
    <t s="42">meaning,</t>
    <t s="43">that the beginning of prayer is in a manner of "walk after Havayah your G-d,"</t>
    <t s="44">"after Havayah" meaning below Havayah,</t>
    <t s="45">and in an aspect of "backsides" and externality alone,</t>
    <t s="46">which is the service in a manner of accepting the yoke.</t>
    <t s="47">But the end and purpose of the service is to be "I will behold Your face,"</t>
    <t s="48">in an aspect of inwardness,</t>
    <t s="49">"before Havayah,"</t>
    <t s="50">meaning above Havayah.</t>
    <t s="51">And these two matters in prayer, whose totality is accepting the yoke and perception,</t>
    <t s="52">come about through the two modes of service in the matter of charity,</t>
    <t s="53">one who gives a coin to a poor person and one who appeases him.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
